questionText:
Let $A$ be a priority queue for maintaining a set of elements. Suppose $A$ is implemented using a max-heap data structure. The operation $\text{EXTRACT-MAX}(A)$ extracts and deletes the maximum element from $A$. The operation $\text{INSERT}(A, key)$ inserts a new element $key$ in $A$. The properties of a max-heap are preserved at the end of each of these operations.

When $A$ contains $n$ elements, which one of the following statements about the worst case running time of these two operations is TRUE?
options: $\text{EXTRACT-MAX}(A)$ runs in $O(1)$ whereas $\text{INSERT}(A, key)$ runs in $O(n)$.
$\text{EXTRACT-MAX}(A)$ runs in $O(1)$ whereas $\text{INSERT}(A, key)$ runs in $O(\log(n))$.
explanation:
Step 1: Analyze EXTRACT-MAX operation
In a max-heap of size $n$, the maximum element is located at the root. The $\text{EXTRACT-MAX}(A)$ operation removes the root element, replaces it with the last element of the heap, and then performs a heapify-down operation to restore the max-heap property.
In the worst case, the replaced element travels down from the root to a leaf node along the height of the tree. Since the height of a binary heap with $n$ elements is $\lfloor\log_2(n)\rfloor$, the worst-case running time of $\text{EXTRACT-MAX}(A)$ is $O(\log(n))$.

Step 2: Analyze INSERT operation
The $\text{INSERT}(A, key)$ operation places the new element at the bottom-rightmost position (end of the array implementation) and performs a heapify-up operation to restore the max-heap property.
In the worst case, the newly inserted key travels up from the leaf to the root node along the height of the tree. Thus, the worst-case running time of $\text{INSERT}(A, key)$ is also $O(\log(n))$.

Conclusion:
Both operations have a worst-case time complexity of $O(\log(n))$. Therefore, statement (B) is TRUE.
